content:
Hi,

I've implemented a Datastar SDK in Lean https://github.com/carlohamalainen/datastar-lean and my next step is to implement streaming compression. Specifically, we have long running SSE responses and we need to be able to flush the compressed stream so that events reach the user's browser immediately.

brotli

I can't find any packages. I guess I could do my own FFI to the C library. This would only need the encoding side.

zstd

This looks like it ticks all my boxes: https://github.com/kim-em/lean-zstd

zlib

https://github.com/kim-em/lean-zlib supports streaming (side note, their other repo https://github.com/kim-em/lean-zip is also interesting but doesn't have streaming support).

Have I missed any libraries?

And from a packaging perspective, would it make sense to keep the compression libraries separate? This is what I did in the Haskell SDK https://github.com/starfederation/datastar-haskell which has sub-packages datastar-hs-brotli, datastar-hs-zlib, datastar-hs-zstd to reduce build dependencies on end users.

Cheers,

Carlo
I believe @Kim Morrison has implementations for zip, zlip, zstd, brotli?
I have these and a few more linked on my site https://leangineer.com/awesome/cryptography-compression/
